title: Implement lore query --across-refs: the read-only cross-ref view (DEC-40 / ODOC-330)
description:
Implement lore's half of the read-only cross-ref view ruled by DEC-40 (operator, first-party, 2026-09-29), which accepted the LCLI-651 proposal's D1-D6 exactly as recommended: D1 gh shell-out behind `src/adapters/forge.ts`; D2 per-hit key `refProvenance` (quest-cli renames its unshipped key to match, so the key is identical across both CLIs); D3 fetch discovered PR heads, objects only; D4 no `lore read` this release; D5 ref-local scores with dev ordered first; D6 no ref cap, with the cost measured at qualification.

Binding ADR: opum-doc `docs/adr/keep-lore-and-quest-records-on-the-branch-with-a-read-only-view-across-open-prs.md` (ODOC-330, accepted 2026-09-29), read by ref there — not from this record.

The operator's condition, part of the choice and additional to the six: with no `gh` on PATH, or a non-GitHub `origin` remote, `--across-refs` reports incomplete coverage (exit 6) and NEVER errors out — a classified outcome, never an uncaught failure.

Shared bytes with quest-cli (their side: QCLI-417), confirmed by cross-session message 2026-09-29 with three deltas, all recorded: (1) the dev ref's spelling is `origin/dev`, taking theirs over my note's `refs/heads/dev`; (2) `refsRead` entries are the inner provenance object verbatim and `refsUnreadable` entries are `{ref, pullRequest, reason}` — richer than the string arrays my proposal sent opum-agent, so those shapes supersede it; (3) lore's `error_type` is its own closed published taxonomy (cli-contract §5.3), so an incomplete run is `drift` (exit 6) with the coverage object in the envelope's `input`, not quest's `coverage_incomplete` — raised to opum-agent as a named divergence rather than absorbed.

Out of scope on purpose: no release and no tag (the pair release gets its own dispatch once both halves land and opum-cli-e2e qualifies them); no `lore read` support (D4); no ref cap (D6); `lore sync` must never accept the flag (ADR decision 6 — a branch's managed blocks regenerate only from that branch's own records).

acceptanceCriteria.text: `lore query --across-refs` returns one row per (id, ref) observation, each hit carrying `refProvenance` {ref, pullRequest, sha} — ref `origin/dev` or `refs/pull/<N>/head`, pullRequest `owner/repo#N` or null, sha the full 40-hex commit actually read — proven against a fixture repository whose refs are real git objects.

`coverage` is a top-level envelope key placed after `data` and before `principal` on every `--across-refs` result, with refsRead entries as inner provenance objects and refsUnreadable entries as {ref, pullRequest, reason}, and `complete` always relative to the population named in the same object.
Exit codes are exactly 0 when every ref in the population was read, 6 naming the unreadable refs when not, 3 when `origin` or `origin/dev` is absent, and never 5 for content conflicts.

With no `gh` on PATH, or a non-GitHub `origin` remote, `--across-refs` produces the classified incomplete-coverage outcome (exit 6) and never an uncaught failure; under `--allow-partial` the same run exits 0 with complete:false and population "dev-only", and dev-only never appears with complete:true.

`--across-refs <ref>` (repeatable) reads exactly the named refs by local resolution with no fetch and no forge call, population "explicit"; mixing bare and valued forms, `--allow-partial` without `--across-refs`, and `--across-refs` with `--workspace`/`--repository` are usage errors (exit 2).

The row rule is exactly as ruled: dev's observation of an id always emits a row, another ref's observation emits a row only when its file bytes differ from dev's, an id absent from dev emits one row per ref carrying it — nothing merged and no winner picked, so a divergent copy appears as several rows with the same id.

The view never writes to the working tree or the index (byte-identical `git status` and index across a run), never reads the working tree for its answer, and `lore sync` plus every mutating command rejects the flag.

Proof both ways with versions resolved: each new behaviour's test fails against the pre-change build and passes against the changed one, and the record names the lore (from source), `gh` and `git` versions the proof ran with.

plan: 1. Branch off dev and read the seams the view hooks into: query arg parsing and flag gating, the workspace-provenance stamping path, the envelope constructor, and the manifest query entry.

2. Implement src/adapters/forge.ts (gh discovery behind an injectable seam, never throwing) and src/core/cross-ref.ts (resolve refs -> fetch objects -> materialize -> per-ref reference load -> merge rows -> coverage).
3. Wire the command surface: query.ts flags + refProvenance stamping, args.ts selection, manifest.ts flags and exit codes, output.ts top-level coverage, core/query.ts hit type.
4. Tests against fixture repositories with real git refs, a stub gh on PATH for discovery, and assertions for exits, coverage, conflict rows and the no-write guarantee.
5. Local gates (bun test, lint, typecheck, bun run lore check), then independent review and proof both ways with lore/gh/git versions resolved.
6. Land the PR with the acceptance criteria checked and the task closed in it; report to opum-agent.
implementationNotes: SHARED-BYTES RESOLUTION, 2026-09-29 (cross-session with quest-cli, who builds QCLI-417 in parallel). The third delta DISSOLVED instead of needing a ruling: quest's error_type is ALSO a closed union and also lacks coverage_incomplete (their src/domain/command-contract.ts:22-29), so adding it would have cost two published-taxonomy changes, not one. Agreed shape, literal parity with no contract change on either side: exit 6, error_type "drift", the coverage object and the failing refs in the error envelope's input, and the message naming the unreadable refs. Also measured and agreed: at exit 6 BOTH sides emit only the error envelope on stderr with stdout empty (quest measured it on an exit-3 case and an exit-6 case), so there is no second divergence. refsUnreadable.reason is free text with the shared sanitisation guarantee: single line, no absolute paths. Deltas 1 and 2 stand as taken: the dev ref's spelling is "origin/dev" (the ADR's own, over my note's refs/heads/dev), and refsRead entries are the inner provenance object while refsUnreadable entries are {ref, pullRequest, reason} — objects rather than the string arrays my LCLI-651 proposal told opum-agent, so those shapes supersede it. This removes the only open question I had raised upward.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE on branch feat/LCLI-652-across-refs (PR #429, head a8578a34). Shape as ruled: forge seam in src/adapters/forge.ts (gh shell-out, injectable spawn, never throws); src/core/cross-ref.ts does discovery -> per-ref read -> merge -> coverage; query.ts wires the flags and stamps refProvenance; output.ts grew an optional envelope extension so coverage sits after data and before principal; manifest declares --across-refs (optionalValue, repeatable) and --allow-partial on query only, plus the git seam. Reading another ref: destination-less 'git fetch --no-tags origin <refspec>' (objects + FETCH_HEAD only, verified no ref appears), then 'git archive --format=zip -0 <sha> docs' parsed in-process by src/zip-store.ts's existing parseStoreZip (no tar dependency; verified on a real archive before building on it) into a temp dir loaded by the same loader every read uses, removed in a finally.

FOUR DESIGN DECISIONS TAKEN WITHIN THE RULING, each named rather than silent:
(a) A ref that was READ and carries no bundle at all contributes zero rows and stays in refsRead with coverage complete — it is an answer, not a failure. The alternative (treat it as unreadable) would make one branch predating docs/ fail the whole view with exit 6. Pinned by its own test.
(b) The explicit population anchors on a ref named 'origin/dev' or 'dev' when one is among the named refs, and reorders it first, so the identical question asked two ways (bare --across-refs versus naming origin/dev and a PR head explicitly) yields the same rows.
(c) A search text that follows --across-refs is refused as a usage error naming what happened, because Commander hands it to the flag (measured) and a git ref name cannot contain whitespace.
(d) src/cli.ts HAD A REAL BUG this work exposed: an optional-value flag given bare reaches the option event as null (not undefined), and normalizeCommandArgs re-serialized it as the literal '--across-refs=null' — a bare flag became a ref named null, and the run then exited 6 on a repo with no origin instead of 3. Both option handlers now test the value's type.

PROOF, both ways, versions resolved: git 2.55.0, gh 2.101.0, bun 1.3.14 locally (CI pins 1.4.2), lore 0.11.0 from source. 26/26 new tests green; full suite 4848 pass / 1 skip / 1 fail where the failure is the pre-existing local-Bun floor check (test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts asserts the pinned runtime is >= 1.4.2) and is unrelated to the diff. Mutants, each reddening only its own mechanism: collapse rule disabled -> exactly 1 test (the collapse/divergence case); CLI option guard reverted to the old definedness test -> the 4 CLI-path bare-flag tests; bundle-less-ref rule made strict -> exactly 1 test. One mutant (treating EVERY ref as bundle-less) reddened 8 — recorded as a blanket mutant that proves only that the read path is exercised, not counted as localisation evidence.

NAMED, NOT ABSORBED, for the orchestrator: opum-agent's relay of the operator's remedy said the no-origin and non-GitHub cases must BOTH assert exit 6. The accepted agreement (quest-cli's exit list, recorded on LCLI-651) puts an ABSENT origin/origin-dev at exit 3 and the non-GitHub/gh-missing discovery failure at exit 6; the tests assert exactly that, and the exit list is a shared cross-CLI contract, so moving it is a joint ruling rather than a silent local change.
finalSummary:
Implemented lore's half of DEC-40 / ODOC-330 exactly as the LCLI-651 proposal shaped it and as the operator ruled D1-D6, with the shared bytes agreed with quest-cli (QCLI-417). `lore query --across-refs` reads origin/dev plus every open pull request into dev (bare) or exactly the named refs (valued, resolved locally, no forge); every hit carries `refProvenance` {ref, pullRequest, sha}; every answer carries top-level `coverage` {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead[], refsUnreadable[]} between `data` and `principal`; conflicting copies of an id are shown side by side and never merged (dev's row always, another ref's only when its bytes differ, an id absent from dev one row per carrying ref, dev first, ref-local scores). Nothing is written: other refs are read with a destination-less, `--refmap=`-pinned `git fetch` (objects and FETCH_HEAD only) and `git archive --format=zip -0`, parsed in-process by the existing store-zip reader (no tar dependency) into a temporary directory loaded by the same loader every other read uses; each ref is read with its OWN profile, and `lore sync` refuses the flag. Exits 0 complete / 6 incomplete as `drift` with the coverage object at `input.coverage` and nothing on stdout / 3 when origin or origin/dev is absent / never 5; `--allow-partial` answers at 0 with complete:false, and no gh or a non-GitHub origin degrades to population dev-only the same way rather than erroring out.

VERIFIED, both ways and with controls. 32 tests in test/cross-ref.test.ts, including the operator-mandated fixtures for a repository with no origin and for a non-GitHub origin (the remote is written into .git/config by the fixture, never a shell `git remote add`), each asserting exit 6, drift, input.coverage and zero bytes on stdout. Full suite 4855 pass / 1 skip / 1 fail, the failure being the pre-existing local-Bun floor check (test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts asserts the pinned 1.4.2 runtime; this workstation runs 1.3.14) and unrelated to the diff. Four mutants, each reddening only its own mechanism: collapse rule disabled -> 1 test; CLI option guard reverted -> the 4 bare-flag CLI tests; bundle-less-ref rule made strict -> 1 test; `--refmap=` removed -> exactly the test that pins it. Versions resolved: git 2.55.0, gh 2.101.0, bun 1.3.14 locally (CI pins 1.4.2), lore 0.11.0 from source.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW, and what it changed. An adversarial review of a8578a34 returned seven findings; the highest-severity one was CONFIRMED first-party with the control in the same invocation: a destination-less refspec does NOT keep a fetch to FETCH_HEAD only — git applies the remote's configured fetch spec, so `git fetch origin dev` advanced refs/remotes/origin/dev (ff1d4fae -> fe3f584e), making the documented "the view never writes" false in the one place nobody would look. Fixed with `--refmap=` at d2b26ce4, pinned by a test that asserts the remote-tracking ref does not move while the commit read is the remote's tip, and re-proven by removing the flag. Also fixed from that review: the per-ref query inherited the engine's default cap of 20 and silently truncated a ref before the merge (now uncapped per ref, capped on the merged listing, pinned by a 25-match fixture); the drift error's input was the coverage object itself where quest-cli emits input.coverage (nested); refsUnreadable reasons could embed git stderr's absolute paths; the ref's own profile now reaches the query as well as the loader, and .lore/profile.json is archived with the TOML form; `lore help query` renders the optional value; and the spawn/fs calls on the classified-failure paths are guarded so a PATH without git cannot escape as an uncaught exit 1.

A SECOND, independent VERIFICATION pass over a8578a34..d2b26ce4 verified six of the seven fixes by measurement and REFUTED the seventh: a backslash-only UNC path survived the POSIX-only reason scrubber byte-identical, reachable end-to-end because git echoes the configured remote URL on any platform. Rather than tune the pattern, the fetch path no longer copies git's stderr at all — `classifyFetchFailure` maps it to a closed phrase, so nothing never copied can leak — with the scrubber kept as belt-and-braces for lore's own messages, its known residue documented, discovery-failure reasons passed through it, and the cleanup/write paths guarded. Both passes' findings are in the branch commits d2b26ce4 and 9e84f46a; the CI run that validated the deliverable is 36585759369 on 9e84f46a, twelve contexts success plus `promotion is manual` skipped by design, and the tracker-only closure commit that follows it is covered by the merge gate on the pull request's final head. Landed as opum-ai/lore-cli#429.
